definitions.explanation: A raised structure used for observation and surveillance, historically built in castles and military fortifications for spotting approaching enemies. Also used figuratively.

examples.japanese: ⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{物見櫓|ものみやぐら}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{遠|とお}く⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見渡|みわた}せる→見渡す：07169_miwatasu⟧。
examples.english: You can see far into the distance from the castle's watchtower.

examples.japanese: {物見櫓|ものみやぐら}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登|のぼ}って→登る：00660_noboru⟧⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{動|うご}き→動き：11926_ugoki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{監視|かんし}→監視：05521_kanshi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: They climbed the watchtower and monitored the enemy's movements.

examples.japanese: ⟦{復元|ふくげん}→復元：09249_fukugen⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧{物見櫓|ものみやぐら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中心|ちゅうしん}→中心：01467_chuushin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{建|た}っている→建つ：12544_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: A reconstructed watchtower stands at the center of the historical park.

notes:
USAGE:
Composed of {物見|ものみ} (watching, lookout) + ⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧ (tower, turret). Primarily associated with Japanese castles and historical settings. The word ⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧ alone also appears in other compounds like {太鼓櫓|たいこやぐら} (drum tower) and {火|ひ}の{見|み}⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧ (fire lookout tower).

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧: tower, turret
- ⟦{天守閣|てんしゅかく}→天守閣：17449_tenshukaku⟧: castle keep, main tower of a Japanese castle
- {火|ひ}の{見|み}⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧: fire watchtower — once common in Japanese towns for spotting fires
